articles.title: Frontier AI labs say their models refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis. What does that mean? | TechCrunch
articles.summary: TechCrunch spoke to the MIT computer scientist charged with explaining OpenAI's latest mind-bending discovery.
articles.body_text: OpenAI released solutions to three blockbuster math problems that have long vexed researchers. One was a surprise rejection of the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), a durable assumption in computer science that plays a large role in how we understand what is difficult to compute. As with previous proof-drops from the frontier lab, scientific communities responded with a mixture of thrill and dismay. Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge suggested that OpenAI was basing its solutions on pre-existing work, and hours later, Anthropic subsequently released its own refutation of ETH. However, OpenAI’s process is evolving. This time, the lab structured its releases differently for each of the three disciplines involved: Mathematicians got the work dropped on GitHub; the computer scientists formed a working group, asked for the proofs to be shared publicly and OpenAI to fund a conference to discuss them; the physicists formed a working group that will determine how their result will be released. MIT professor Ryan Williams is the computer scientist who is organizing his field’s response to the new finding. Williams, whose work focuses on these questions of computational complexity, has criticized OpenAI’s approach in the past, calling its proof dump earlier this October a “DDOS attack on mathematicians.” However, he agreed to collaborate with the frontier labs in order to help shepherd ideas that are vital to the field, he told TechCrunch. The lab asked him to help interpret the solution, along with UC San Diego computer scientists Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi, who first published the ETH in 1999. Their first step was to release an open letter calling for feedback from scientists interested in these problems and a discussion of the norms around AI contributions to their work. “Some parts [of OpenAI’s proof] are, maybe you could say routine, but then yes, there are two or three alien-looking parts, and it’s exactly these parts that I saw that made me think, wow, this is something that the whole community needs to work on together,” Williams told TechCrunch. The ETH is part of a broader class of problems known as P versus NP, which has animated computer science and many other fields for decades. Reductively, researchers are trying to understand if any problem whose solution can be easily verified (NP) can also be easily solved (P). A simple example is the game Sodoku: Once a solution to a puzzle is in place, it can be quickly verified, but finding the solution is time-consuming. That dynamic is true across a range of important problems, and the insight underpins cryptographic systems: When you have the key to an encoded message, you can reveal it, but actually cracking an effective code takes too long to be useful. However, scientists have yet to prove whether that is always true. “P = NP is saying that, not only can you verify Sudoku solutions when they exist, you can just generate them,” Williams said. “P = NP is asserting that this is true for every single problem you can verify quickly — if you can verify it quickly, you can solve it quickly. So this just seems too good to be true.” That’s why most scientists assume that P ≠ NP. ETH provided evidence for that. It basically says that even the fastest computer algorithm needs exponentially more time to find a solution as the number of variables grow in a specific class of tricky logic puzzle. The claims from OpenAI and Anthropic is that their models have come up with algorithms that solve those puzzles in “sub-exponential” time, meaning faster than the speeds previously thought possible. If true, they may have proven the EFT to be false — refuted it, in scientific terms — and maybe opened up a path for algorithms that generally perform P = NP.

articles.title: Exclusive: Meta director Rohit Patel departs after 8 years to take on Microsoft Office Suite
articles.summary: Rohit Patel is departing Meta after eight years working on AI evaluations and reinforcement learning, TechCrunch has exclusively learned. His startup, Ndoc, aims to take on Microsoft Office Suite.
articles.body_text: After eight years developing AI for Meta, Rohit Patel is departing the company, TechCrunch has exclusively learned. The former director at Meta Superintelligence Labs has launched Ndoc , a startup he’s pitching as an AI-native replacement for Microsoft Office suite or Google Workspace. Patel is the latest in a handful of high-profile departures from Meta following the exits of Chief Global Affairs Officer Joel Kaplan , AI researcher Andrew Tulloch , and Head of Product for AI-for-Work Emily Dalton Smith . Patel designed Ndoc to be more than just another AI tool layered onto an existing workflow. The goal is to replace the fragmented way people work across tools like Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Tableau, Replit, and “ChatGPT copy-paste” with one unified workspace that all colleagues can access, even if they’re not signed up for Ndoc. Ndoc brings three components together in one layout. The Stage tab is where presentations of key findings live, like slide decks, dashboards, simulations, or mini apps. The Narrative tab features analyses, numbered citations, generated figures, and generally the “why” behind the numbers. The Model tab is where underlying datasets and Python scripts are housed. The design reflects Patel’s background. During his tenure at Meta, Patel focused on reinforcement learning — a type of machine learning in which AI agents learn to make decisions through trial and error and maximize rewards — and evaluating whether AI output is trustworthy. Patel believes that if AI is going to build the spreadsheets and slide decks that companies use to make decisions, someone should be able to check its work. For instance, users can find the Python scripts used to create the documents. “Even if you don’t know any Python, you can ask [the AI chat] to explain, ‘Hey, what does this script do? Which line has my formula?’ And you can verify that formula,” Patel said. “There’s nothing hidden behind the curtain here.” In practice, users can upload a dataset and ask Ndoc to perform an analysis and write a narrative about the findings. They can also add document-specific context, including audience, tone, and memory. “It maintains a memory across your person, that particular document, your team, and your company,” Patel said. Patel also says Ndoc is built and fine-tuned using a mixture of open source models. Because the platform was developed from scratch, he says it costs considerably less to run than alternatives built on frontier AI models. “I thought that’s what people would be excited about, but people don’t care about that,” he said, referring to his early trial users. “What people are excited about is that they love seeing all their end-to-end in one place.” Patel’s larger ambition is to reinvent the file itself. He says documents can be exported as a single “.ndoc.html” file that can be opened in any browser, a format he plans to open-source so other developers can build apps that work with it without being locked into Ndoc the way so many have been locked into Microsoft or Google for years. His desire to open-source this project was partly why he left Meta and decided to go it alone. At a big company like Meta, getting everyone to agree on an open source format would undoubtedly require the input of “hundreds of people and opinions on how the format should look.” Patel wanted to move quickly. “Humans can only move at human pace, whereas…I can move at the pace of what AI can do.”

articles.title: Billionaire Palmer Luckey isn't leaving California over the wealth tax | TechCrunch
articles.summary: "It's causing a lot of people to run who I don't want to be running," native Californian Palmer Luckey said. "But I'm planning on staying in California. I'm going to keep fighting it."
articles.body_text: Palmer Luckey has been a California billionaire since he was 21 years old, when he sold his first company, virtual reality headset maker Oculus VR, to Facebook for $2 billion in 2014. His current company, defense tech firm Anduril, is headquartered in Costa Mesa, California, not far from Long Beach, where Luckey grew up. And Anduril is worth far more. It was last valued at $61 billion. While Luckey clearly despises the proposed California billionaire wealth tax, a ballot measure that would tax the net worth of the state’s richest residents, he said he’s not leaving California over it. “I think that this tax act, if you can call it a tax, is going to cause a lot of problems. It’s causing a lot of people to run who I don’t want to be running. It’s going to cause companies that I work with to leave the state, which is a problem for me. As of right now, though, I’m not running. I am staying. I think California is something special. I want to fight for California,” Luckey said during an invite-only press conference on Monday. He added that he’s felt pressure from other billionaires to declare his intention to leave. “This has been a point of friction between me and some of my other billionaire friends,” he said. “They’ve said things like ‘Palmer, you have to have solidarity for us. You can’t enable these really bad policies. If you stay and if you don’t leave, it’s going to show them that there’s no consequences.’ I empathize with that argument, but it’s not one that I’m going to participate in right now because I still believe that we can fix things.” Luckey added that it’s not the idea of paying taxes that he takes issue with, but that the bill is sponsored by a specific union, a unit of the United Healthcare Workers , that wants to use the money the tax would raise “for their uses,” he said. The measure’s sponsors say the money will be used for “health care, education, and food assistance” programs in the state, and they specifically name Medi-Cal, California’s health coverage program for low-income residents. Another issue for Luckey, as for others, is how the proposal would assess the tax owed, as well as the penalties. It would tax “wealth” including unrealized assets that haven’t been sold, and illiquid assets that are hard to turn into cash. And penalties can be assessed as high as 40%. “It’s almost like a seizure of future wealth in that way. That’s not even the real problem. The biggest problem is the tax on control of your own company,” he said. According to the Tax Foundation, a tax policy think tank, the proposal would treat someone with voting control as owning at least that same share of the company. This would affect founders with super-voting shares, which carry extra votes per share, because they may own only a minority of the company. A founder with 40% of the votes but 10% of the ownership, for example, could be taxed as if they owned at least 40%, and selling all their shares might not cover the bill. (The measure’s drafters say that reading is mistaken, arguing that super-voting shares are publicly traded assets and are valued differently.) “I’m a founder who’s raised a bunch of money, I’ve diluted myself a lot. I’ve given equity to my employees,” Luckey said of his own situation. “My employees have more equity in Anduril than me. I’ve given a lot of equity out to people, but what I have done is I’ve preserved the voting rights so that as those employees sell their shares to pay off their home loans or whatever, that the voting control doesn’t go to other people outside the company.” He also said that if he were ever to leave, “I lose all those voting rights. My voting rights only stick as long as I’m an American citizen living in America, running Anduril.” The condition makes sense given that Anduril is primarily a defense contractor selling equipment to the U.S. military. In Luckey’s case, he believes he could owe 5% of Anduril’s $61 billion, a bill of around $3 billion, just on that asset alone. (For comparison, Larry Page, the Google co-founder who did leave California, still has 27% voting control of Alphabet , Google’s parent company, which has a market value of just under $4 trillion.) “But I’m planning on staying in California. I’m going to keep fighting it,” he said. “I’m hoping that this doesn’t pass. I’m hoping if it does pass, that there are legal challenges to say, ‘Hey, you can’t post facto seize people’s past and future wealth, nor can you tax their voting interests in their own company.’ That’s truly unprecedented. That is not a tax on ownership. It is a tax on control.”

articles.title: Anduril, Qualcomm launch BlueChip, a new kind of US-made laptop | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Anduril founder Palmer Luckey is vowing to bring computer manufacturing back to the U.S., and by that he doesn't just mean assembly, but every individual component, some of which are exclusively made in China today.
articles.body_text: Anduril founder Palmer Luckey is vowing to bring computer manufacturing back to the U.S. And by that, he doesn’t just mean assembly, but the production of every individual component, some of which are exclusively made in China today. Anduril is partnering with Qualcomm to achieve that mission with a new computer called BlueChip, the companies announced Tuesday. BlueChip will be available for preorder in 2027. While technical details are scant — Anduril hasn’t even finished contracting with all its component suppliers yet, according to Luckey — this first product will be a hardened laptop. It will be designed to withstand the most grueling physical environments and meet the security-conscious needs of the military, government, first responders, and law enforcement. For the first generation, about 90% of its components will be made in the U.S. or in allied countries, Anduril says, most notably its CPU. BlueChip will run on a Snapdragon X Series built at TSMC’s massive new facility in Arizona. The CPU uses the same architecture that powers other laptops, including the Microsoft Surface, Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon said during the press conference. “As of right now, the laptop’s bill of materials is about 90% U.S. and allied [ally countries], and we have a technical roadmap to get to 100% domestic over time,” Luckey said. “The intent in the long run is to have an option that is made entirely in the United States, 100% domestic. And I mean everything. I mean the displays. I mean the metallics. I mean the the magnetics. All of it.” Right now, for instance, Luckey says he’s found an American supplier for the glass that covers the display, but the display itself is one of several components he says are only manufactured in China. While Luckey says consumers are welcome to order a BlueChip — the company may even create a waiting list for interested consumers — this first PC won’t be designed for them. For one thing, as a hardened computer, it will be heavy and have battery-life constraints because of the engineering required to withstand rain, dust, and other rugged conditions. The bigger point is to offer U.S. government agencies a product that complies with regulations requiring them to buy U.S.-made computers. In this case, the selling point is a transparent supply chain that customers can track and audit. “These computers are the anti-surveillance computer. You fully control it,” Luckey described in a recent interview. “You know everything that is in it, every single component, and you know every software component that is running on it.” Anduril is also working to ensure that the Arm-based machine works well with Windows apps, apps built for certain Linux distributions used by the government, and even archaic software that various agencies still run. While Anduril hasn’t yet announced pricing, Luckey estimates it will cost about 20% more than typical high-end PCs. “As much as I love BlueChip, if I was just a normal consumer making a rational decision without a kind of patriotic basis, I’d be better off buying a Dell laptop than an Anduril laptop because it’s going to be cheaper. I’m just talking about your average-person consumer, right, who doesn’t have any real need for this,” Luckey said.

articles.title: General Compute raises $100 million Series A, countering the neocloud disaster narrative | TechCrunch
articles.summary: General Compute is betting on inference chips from outside the Nvidia ecosystem.
articles.body_text: CoreWeave, a publicly traded neocloud that rents out computing power for AI, has seen its stock price fall to a 12-month low, and Elon Musk is flexing $40 billion in debt for buying computing capacity and predicting that “200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation.” It’s not exactly the ideal week to announce a Series A for a neocloud. General Compute co-founder and CEO Finn Puklowski is unfazed. He’s bullish on CoreWeave’s chances, and thinks Musk is just talking his book to drive down the prices of the GPUs he wants to buy. Fears of a chip-led collapse are “massively overstated. I have people calling me up every single week asking me to do TPUs, GPUs, any chip, to get them more compute.” Just as important, he says, Anthropic’s bullish S-1 is “settling fears for today.” General Compute has found a niche building its cloud out of specialized inference chips built by Nvidia rivals. The company struck a $400 million deal to purchase new chips from SambaNova — the first debt financing of inference chips — and now has added Positron and Cerebras to its portfolio of chip suppliers. A deal with a large customer worth $100 million in annual recurring revenue has paved the way for the company to raise $100 million in Series A funding led by Blackbird Ventures and Abstract Ventures. Valued at $60 million after a May seed round , General Compute is now worth $800 million post-money to its investors. The startup’s strategy is to zig where others zag. It focused on chips built for inference while everyone else chased GPUs. And instead of taking on a complex effort to build huge data centers, it uses smaller power sources, rents space in other companies’ data centers, and converts former bitcoin-mining sites into places that run AI models. That approach means General Compute isn’t going to catapult into the top ranks of neoclouds or compete with hyperscalers any time soon. But it’s also not subject to the constraints that come with building data centers from scratch. When General Compute has chips, it will have someplace to plug them in. Puklowski expects the company to deploy 75 megawatts of computing capacity in 2027, and he suspects he will have access to 200 megawatts of power — “more than we can probably fund and get hardware for.” Still, the plan has a limit. Puklowski’s financing work isn’t done — “capital is going to be a full-time job for me, both on debt and equity,” he told TechCrunch. The startup has found key customers in cloud companies that specialize in offering developers high-speed inference; General Compute provides the bare metal, or raw servers with no software layered on top, for them to bring their offerings to market. James Palmer, a principal at Blackbird who co-led the round, said his firm’s confidence in General Compute comes in part from an investment in Baseten, an inference cloud company. “We’ve been proximate to their journey over the last 10 months and observing the wild growth story that [Baseten] has gone on, and the demand for open weight inference, and for companies owning their own intelligence,” Palmer told TechCrunch. When it comes to General Compute, he said, “Cerebras, Positron, SambaNova, all need distribution partners who can take them to scale, who can navigate the complexity of the physical world.” Executives at all three chipmakers sang General Compute’s praises to TechCrunch, each noting the importance of the company’s focus on making the economics of AI cloud compute work. “Everyone in this market is selling speed,” Rodrigo Liang, SambaNova’s CEO and co-founder, said. “The real question is whether you can make money doing it.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . This doesn’t affect our editorial independence.

articles.title: Pokémon Unite turns monster battles into a team sport
articles.summary: Pokémon Unite on the Nintendo Switch mashes up Pokémon with MOBAs like League of Legends and Dota 2, and a mobile version is launching in September.
articles.body_text: Games like League of Legends and Dota 2 are massively popular, and have been for the better part of a decade. But they can also be impenetrable to new players and viewers: there are so many characters and strategies that figuring out what’s happening on-screen is a huge challenge. The just-launched Pokémon Unite aims to fix that. It doesn’t just add cute monsters to the genre, but also some clever fixes to streamline it and make things more approachable. It’s kind of like a mashup of a strategy game and basketball, but with a Gengar thrown in. For the uninitiated, a MOBA — or multiplayer online battle arena, to use the genre’s unnecessarily long full name — is a five-on-five competition where the goal, usually, is to destroy the opposing team’s base. You do this by forming a squad of characters, each with their own unique abilities, which you use to steadily destroy towers and level up so you can push your way into your opponent’s territory. It’s often slow and methodical, a genre that rewards smart decisions as well as quick reflexes. Unite has many of these elements, including a varied cast of monsters to choose from. Charmander is a good all-around melee fighter, for instance, while Venasaur is better for ranged attacks. There are support characters and ones designed for defense. In a nice twist, many of the creatures will evolve over the course of the match. It’s fun starting out as a squat little Gible and ending the match as an imposing Garchomp. [Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j86TTIMWBYY] But the most interesting aspects of Unite are where it differs from the traditional MOBA. For starters, instead of trying to destroy your opponents’ base, you’re scoring points. To do this, you have to defeat wild pokémon that spawn throughout the arena to earn points, which you then take to one of the opponent’s goal circles to score. Drop enough points to destroy a circle and you can move on to the next. It’s similar to how MOBAs usually work, but it’s also a lot simpler to understand. And the system also adds some new drama: if you’re killed, you’ll lose a big chunk of the points you’re holding, which makes things very tense if you have a lot stacked up. The other nice thing about the game is that it has a strict time limit. Whereas a League of Legends match can stretch to close to an hour if it’s tightly contested, a single Pokémon Unite match takes exactly 10 minutes. Once the timer runs down, whichever team has the most points wins. (Some matches can actually be shorter; I’ve already played a few where the other team forfeited early because of a lopsided score.) The time limit and points system make Unite feel a bit more like a virtual sport, albeit one with experience points and spawning monsters. This idea of streamlining a MOBA isn’t exactly new. Blizzard tried it with Heroes of the Storm, and Riot did something similar when it brought League of Legends to mobile with the spinoff Wild Rift. But, at least from what I’ve played so far, Unite seems the most approachable. The rules are easy to understand, the matches are short and intense, and the world is already something millions of people know and love. So far, the only real issue I’ve run into is the copious amounts of virtual currency you can earn or buy. It gets weirdly complicated, to the point that you can spend as much time messing around in battle pass menus as actually playing the game. It doesn’t seem like you have to buy anything, but some of the fashion options are pretty tempting. Right now, Pokémon Unite is available as a free download on the Nintendo Switch, but it’s poised to become even bigger when it debuts on mobile in September (with crossplay and cross progression at launch). Developer TiMi, an internal studio at Tencent, already operates two of the biggest games in the world with Call of Duty: Mobile and Honor of Kings. The combination of Pokémon and MOBA could soon add a third.

articles.title: Vapenhotet mot Trump: Förgör USA
articles.summary: Kim Jong-Un riktar vapenhot mot Donald Trump. Den nordkoreanske diktatorn hotar ”förgöra” USA.
articles.body_text: Kim Jong-Un riktar vapenhot mot Donald Trump. Den nordkoreanske diktatorn hotar ”förgöra” USA, skriver Telegraph . Sydkorea anklagas också för vad som beskrivs som ”ondskefulla” försök. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Nordkoreas diktator Kim Jong-Un har placerat ut tre haubitsar nära gränsen till Sydkorea. Under vapnen står det skrivet: ”Förgör de amerikanska imperialistiska angriparna, det koreanska folkets svurna fiender!” Experter noterade att det är ovanligt att Nordkorea visar upp artilleri på ett så iögonfallande sätt. – Vår uppfattning är att Nordkorea har placerat ut äldre artilleri längs kustområden i tydlig synlighet. Även om Nordkorea har nämnt nya vapensystem i sina senaste uttalanden anser vi att detta inte kan betraktas som sådant, säger kapten Jang Do-young, talesperson för Sydkoreas militärledning. Spänningarna mellan Nordkorea och Sydkorea har varit höga efter att en minexplosion vid gränsen skadade tre sydkoreanska soldater i september. Sydkorea har anklagat grannlandet för att ligga bakom explosionen och krävt en ursäkt, men Nordkorea har vägrat och kommit med motanklagelser. På måndagen meddelade nordkoreanska statliga medier att landet har lämnat in ett klagomål till FN:s säkerhetsråd angående vad man beskriver som ”ett ondskefullt försök att hindra och försena Nordkoreas befästning av den södra gränsen”, något man beskrev som en ”självförsvarsåtgärd”. Kim Yo-Jong, Kim Jong-Uns syster, sade förra veckan att Nordkorea kommer att börja sprida anti-sydkoreansk propaganda i högtalare längs gränsen. USA är en av Sydkoreas främsta allierade. Donald Trump träffade Kim Jong-Un under sin första mandatperiod som president och har sagt att han vill ha ett nytt möte med den nordkoreanske ledaren, men detta har hittills fallit för döva öron. – Jag kommer väldigt bra överens med honom, och jag är inte säker på att någon ber om ett möte, har Trump sagt om Kim.

articles.title: Utvisas i chartrat plan – är dömda för brott
articles.summary: Ett chartrat flygplan väntas under natten lyfta från Arlanda med ett tiotal somalier som ska utvisas från Sverige ombord. Enligt uppgifter till Expressen har insatsen planerats under stort hemlighetsmakeri.
articles.body_text: Ett chartrat flygplan väntas under natten lyfta från Arlanda med ett tiotal somalier som ska utvisas från Sverige ombord. Enligt uppgifter till Expressen har insatsen planerats under stort hemlighetsmakeri. Det är det senaste försöket att genomföra utvisningarna efter flera tidigare misslyckanden. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Flera av personerna som omfattas av utvisningen är dömda för brott, enligt Expressens uppgifter. Men det är inte brottsligheten som ligger bakom utvisningsbesluten. I stället ska skälet vara att personerna har lämnat oriktiga uppgifter när de kom till Sverige, bland annat om sin identitet och klantillhörighet. Det är inte första gången på senare tid som svenska myndigheter försöker genomföra tvångsutvisningar till Somalia . I slutet av september stoppades ett försök sedan medpassagerare protesterat ombord på ett reguljärflyg. Piloten vägrade till slut att lyfta, rapporterade Aftonbladet . Den 14 oktober stoppades ytterligare en planerad utvisning från Arlanda, sedan somaliska myndigheter sagt nej. Beskedet kom efter Sveriges Radios avslöjande om en omstridd överenskommelse mellan Sverige och Somalia, där svenska biståndspengar ska ha gått till projekt med kopplingar till landets premiärminister. I utbyte ska Somalia ha gått med på att ta emot tvångsutvisade medborgare. Enligt Dagens Nyheters källor bedömdes läget som alltför känsligt för att låta flyget lyfta. För att undvika samma tumult som uppstod vid försöket i september har nattens plan chartrats särskilt för utvisningarna, enligt Expressens uppgifter.

articles.title: Gick ut med hunden – dog
articles.summary: Sal Galloway var ute med hunden. Då sveptes 59-åringen ut till havs. Hennes liv kunde inte räddas.
articles.body_text: Hennes liv kunde inte räddas, skriver The Sun . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. 59-åriga Sal Galloway var ute och rastade sin hund längs en strandpromenad på Isle of Wight under måndagen. När Galloway försvann inleddes en omfattande räddningsinsats med kustbevakningen, polis, ambulanssjukvårdare och en helikopter. 59-åringen dödförklarades efter att hennes kropp hade hittats i vattnet några timmar senare. Man tror att en jättevåg slog in över land och svepte ut Galloway till havs. Det är oklart om hennes hund hittats. ”Vila i frid, min kära vän Sal Galloway”, skriver en person på sociala medier. En annan var ”så chockad över att höra de tragiska nyheterna”. ”Min bästa barndomsvän. Kommer att sakna dig”, skriver en tredje. articles.title: Försökte hjälpa flicka att begå självmord
articles.summary: Den 14-åriga flickan överlevde med knapp marginal. Nu åtalas en 21-årig svensk man för att ha försökt mörda henne i Wien. Enligt åklagaren ska han ha rest till Österrike och bland annat hjälpt flickan att förbereda ett självmordsförsök.
articles.body_text: Den 14-åriga flickan överlevde med knapp marginal. Nu åtalas en 21-årig svensk man för att ha försökt mörda henne i Wien. Enligt åklagaren ska han ha rest till Österrike och bland annat hjälpt flickan att genomföra ett självmordsförsök. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Flickan var tolv år gammal och bodde i ett familjehem när hon fick kontakt med den svenske mannen. Under två års tid hade de nästan daglig kontakt via Roblox och Discord och utvecklade en nära relation. Samtalen ska framför allt ha kretsat kring flickans självmordstankar. Till slut ska de ha kommit överens om att mannen skulle resa till Österrike för att hjälpa henne att ta sitt liv. Nu har åtal väckts mot den 21-årige svensken för två fall av mordförsök mot den i dag 14-åriga flickan, rapporterar den österrikiska public service-kanalen ORF . Enligt åtalet ska mannen den 26 maj i år ha uppmuntrat henne att ta sitt liv och hjälpt henne med förberedelserna. Hon hittades då livshotande skadad i källaren till sitt bostadshus i Wien . Flickan överlevde tack vare att en annan boende i huset upptäckte henne. Även svensken befann sig i källaren. Enligt åklagaren ska han ha stått och tittat på i flera minuter utan att ingripa. Någon eller några dagar före självmordsförsöket misstänks han också ha skadat flickan allvarligt genom att skära henne i handlederna med en glasskärva.

articles.title: Maken tillät vidriga attacker mot Joanne
articles.summary: Philip Young lät andra män våldta frun Joanne Young. ”Jag blev väldigt chockad”, säger Joanne Young. Nu står fyra tre män inför rätta för sexövergreppen.
articles.body_text: Philip Young lät andra män våldta frun Joanne Young. – Jag blev väldigt chockad, säger Joanne Young. Nu står maken och ytterligare tre män inför rätta för sexövergreppen, skriver Guardian . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Britten Philip Young, 50, gifte sig 2004 med Joanne Young, 49. Paret fick tre barn. – Utifrån sett verkade de vara ett normalt par med ett normalt familjeliv, säger åklagaren Sarah Jones. Men för tre år sedan förstod Joanne Young att hennes äktenskap inte var vad hon hade trott. Medan hon och maken hade sex kände hon ”någon annans hand på min handled”. – Jag blev väldigt chockad. Det fanns en främmande man i mitt hus och jag var naken, har Joanne Young sagt. Följande morgon erkände maken att han hade bjudit in en person till huset för att titta på dem när de hade sex. Jones sade att Joanne Young, som avstått från sin rätt till anonymitet, inte hade någon aning om allt som hade hänt henne när polisen grep maken. – Den värld hon trodde att hon kände hade helt vänts upp och ner. Relationen hon trodde att hon hade framstår nu som helt overklig, säger Jones. Philip Young och tre män i åldrarna 32, 48 respektive 62 år, som alla bjöds in av honom har åtalats för sexuella övergrepp. Jones berättade för juryn att Joanne Young aldrig gav sitt samtycke till att ha sex med de tre männen.

articles.title: ”Putin paranoid” – nya försvaret vid palatset
articles.summary: Vladimir Putin pekas ut för att vara ”paranoid”. Analyser visar att han förstärker luftvärnet runt sitt palats i den ryska staden Valdai, rapporterar Kyiv Post.
articles.body_text: Vladimir Putin pekas ut för att vara ”paranoid”. Analyser visar att han förstärker luftvärnet runt sitt palats i den ryska staden Valdai, rapporterar Kyiv Post , med hänvisning till data som Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty (RFE/RL) tagit del av. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Den ryska presidenten ökar skyddet vid en av sina bostäder. Det beskrivs av analytiker som det senaste fallet av ”Putins paranoia”. Analys av öppen data som Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty (RFE/RL) tagit del av avslöjar att den ryska presidenten Vladimir Putin låtit bygga en ridå av luftvärnspjäser runt staden Valdai i den nordvästra regionen Novgorod Oblast. Där bor bara 13 600 personer – men en av dem är presidenten själv. Han har sedan flera år tillbaka tagit över det hemliga Sovjet-palatset i staden. I folkmun kallas residenset ”Dolgije Borody”, ungefär ”Långskägget” på svenska. Enligt en utredning av Aleksej Navalnyjs organisation Anti-Corruption Foundation (FBK) innehåller residenset totalt 80 byggnader som sträcker sig över 150 hektar. Den nya luftvärnsväggen sträcker sig från Valdai till två andra viktiga platser: Den intilliggande flygbasen Khotilovo och det hemlighetsfulla biologiska laboratoriet på ön Lisiyj. Totalt har runt 50 luftvärnstorn installerats, enligt satelitbilderna som också OSINT-analytikern Jembob analyserat. Det är inte bekräftat av myndigheter. Byggnationen av luftvärnstornen ska ha varit i gång sedan i mars i år. Den första pjäsen installerades vid flygbasen. Från den går en järnväg raka vägen till Putins ”Dolgije Borody”, skriver Kyiv Post . Putin och Kreml har tidigare anklagat Ukraina för att ha genomfört attacker mot hans residens. I december förra året uppgav ryska myndigheter att de hade skjutit ner fler än 90 sprängladdade drönare som Ukraina avfyrat mot området. Ukraina dementerade uppgifterna, och det bekräftades även senare av amerikanska underrättelser. Enligt CIA var det inte Putins residens som var måltavla för attacken, utan ett militärt mål i regionen långt ifrån bostaden. Detta är en nyhetsartikel. articles.title: Forskare om telefonsamtalet med Putin: ”Han älskar sånt här”
articles.summary: En fantastisk möjlighet för Vladimir Putin att sprida propaganda om kriget och orsaka europeisk splittring, eller början på en seriös diplomatisk process mot fred? Forskare har olika syn på telefonsamtalet mellan ledarna för Norge, Finland och Ryssland.
articles.body_text: En fantastisk möjlighet för Vladimir Putin att sprida propaganda om kriget och orsaka europeisk splittring, eller början på en seriös diplomatisk process mot fred? Forskare har olika syn på telefonsamtalet mellan ledarna för Norge, Finland och Ryssland. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Telefonsamtalet mellan Norges statsminister Jonas Gahr Støre, Finlands president Alexander Stubb och Rysslands president Vladimir Putin var inte koordinerat med andra europeiska ledare. Danmarks statsminister Mette Frederiksen sa att hon var ”mycket skeptisk” till samtalet. Sveriges statsminister Ulf Kristersson säger till Expressen att det vore ”riskabelt” om olika europeiska länder vill ha egna samtal med Ryssland om Ukraina. – Jag tror att man ska ha ganska låg förväntan på den här sortens samtal. Det krävs ett gemensamt europeiskt agerande mot Ryssland. Flemming Splidsboel Hansen, dansk forskare och Rysslandsexpert, anser att samtalet med Putin är problematiskt. – Europa har hela tiden varit överens om att inte ringa Putin. Vi pratar inte med honom såhär, punkt slut. Och så gör vi det ändå. Det är klart att besvikelsen är stor i Danmark, och att det nu blir nordisk och europeisk splittring, säger han till Svenska Dagbladet. Han menar att Putin vill se europeisk splittring och säger att det är ”mycket märkligt” att Gahr Støre och Stubb pratade med den ryske presidenten utan att samordna det med europeiska allierade. – Det här är en fantastisk möjlighet för Putin. Han älskar sånt här. Han älskar när folk närmar sig honom och ber om samtal, säger Flemming Splidsboel Hansen till tidningen. Putin kan genom propaganda framställa det som att Europa nu är berett att göra uppoffringar eftersom man insett att kriget är förlorat. – Det presenteras redan som en stor vinst i ryska medier. Jag ser inte ordet ”ber på sina bara knän” men det är så det kommer att användas i propagandan, säger han till tidningen.

articles.title: Stentuffa straff för tre bröder
articles.summary: Alon, Tal och Oren Alexander levde lyxliv. Nu har de tre bröderna dömts till 30 års fängelse vardera.
articles.body_text: Alon, Tal och Oren Alexander levde lyxliv. Nu har de tre bröderna dömts till 30 års fängelse vardera för sexbrott, skriver CNN . – Min uppfattning om de åtalade är att de var väldigt lika doktor Jekyll och mister Hyde, säger domaren Valerie Caproni. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Tal Alexander, 40, och hans 39-åriga tvillingbröder Oren och Alon Alexander levde lyxliv i New York och Miami, enligt CNN. Tal Alexander och Oren Alexander var toppmäklare inom lyxfastigheter medan Alon Alexander var chef på familjens säkerhetsföretag. Men de dolde en mörk hemlighet. Bröderna åtalades nyligen för att under mer än ett decennium tillsammans och med andra personer ”upprepade gånger droga, sexuellt överfalla och våldta dussintals offer”, enligt justitiedepartementet. – Dessa män har tillbringat år med att behandla kvinnor och flickor som om våra liv, kroppar, röster och mänsklighet inte betydde någonting. Men de kan inte komma undan med det, säger ett offer som använde pseudonymen Katie Moore i rätten. Moore var en av tolv kvinnor som på tisdagen avgav uttalanden i rättssalen i New York fullsatt med offer och deras nära och kära inför domen mot de tre bröderna. Bröderna dömdes vardera till 30 års fängelse för sexhandel och andra brott. Domaren Valerie Caproni liknade de tre bröderna vid doktor Jekyll och mister Hyde efter brödernas vänner beskrev dem som gentlemän medan deras offer beskrev dem som ”sadistiska, kvinnohatande våldtäktsmän”.
